Published dates concern 2026, not 2027. Caveats: French fee page has 2026/27 EUR255 while English page still shows 2025/26 EUR254; language-version lag, not two simultaneous fees. sections.text:
## 5. Université Paris-Saclay, France — M1 Data, Knowledge and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence (DKAI), Master in Computer Science
- Fit: Mathematics bachelor's explicitly accepted alongside CS/engineering/related fields, but strong probability/statistics/algebra/logic, programming (Python/Java/C++), databases and algorithms required. English B2; program marked English. Two-year M1+M2 pathway; applicants after bachelor's should consider M1, not assume M2 access.
- Intake: Latest published program dates are 2026: Inception 15 January–16 March; MonMaster 17 February–16 March. Platform depends on applicant circumstances. 2027 dates not verified.
- Cost/funding: University says eligible non-EU students can receive partial fee exemption bringing differentiated fees to domestic level, under its conditions. Exact DKAI 2027 fee not verified; some programs have special fees. International master's scholarship currently €10,000/year plus up to €900 travel/visa allowance. Foreign nationality, first enrollment in France and under 30 among criteria; coordinators select candidates. Latest 2026 selection deadline was 25 March and scholarship application deadline 31 March; 2027 unannounced in retrieved source.

records.title: MSc Imaging and Light in Extended Reality (IMLEX)
records.institution: University of Eastern Finland / University Jean Monnet / KU Leuven / Toyohashi University of Technology

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: September 2027 entry. Apply 2 December 2026–13 January 2027, 23:59 UTC+2. Verified degree documents due 31 May 2027; graduating applicants final documents by 30 July 2027. 2027 EMJM awards explicitly advertised; application fee waived.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: From 2025 intake onward: non-EU/EEA consortium fee EUR 9,000/year; EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay none. EMJM holders pay no participation fees and receive EUR 1,400/month, maximum 24 months, plus covered insurance/mandatory participation costs. Competitive partial/full fee waivers are separate; living/travel spending is not an assumed zero net cost. Scholarship conditions: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (2027 explicitly offered; amount rules from 2025 onwards): Prior Erasmus Mundus masters award bars a second; no simultaneous Community grant. Full-time physical participation required. EU project nationality-balance rule applies; programme-specific available-country quota not retrieved.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: 2027 criteria explicitly accept mathematics bachelors: recognised institution, at least three full-time years; selection requires ECTS C average or equivalent. Relevant academic preparation is assessed individually.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Imaging, lighting and extended reality

sections.label: Language
sections.text: IELTS Academic 6.5; TOEFL iBT 92 if taken before 21 January 2026, or 4.5 thereafter; PTE 68. Tests must be valid in the application period. English-degree exemptions are country- and delivery-restricted; online/offshore studies outside accepted locations do not qualify.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: No fixed subject-credit minimum published. Maths, physics, algorithms, programming, imaging/XR and electronics inform ranking. Required CV, two references, motivation letter and two-minute video; possible interview. No mandatory work experience or design portfolio stated; this is not a waiver of skills assessment. The admissions page inconsistently calls the video optional in its motivation paragraph but lists it among compulsory enclosures; selection explicitly scores it in round two. Prepare it and verify the live form rather than assume a waiver. Mobility and residence: On-site itinerary: Finland semester 1, France semester 2, Belgium summer school, Japan semester 3; thesis at a partner or industry. Current EU EMJM rules require two 30-ECTS physical periods in different eligible countries, both outside residence at enrolment; verify individual itinerary and visas with the consortium. Award structure: From intake 2025: one joint MSc from UEF, Jean Monnet and KU Leuven, plus Toyohashi national Master of Engineering. Count the integrated IMLEX route once; retain both awards. Scope caveats: Current from-2025 curriculum replaces older Lighting/Computational Imaging tracks; do not count the old tracks again. Distinct from existing MAIA medical-image-analysis programme and from EMJM in Imaging. 2027 maximum intake is 25, subject to programme discretion; admission and scholarship are separate competitive outcomes. No personal probability or nationality eligibility established. Existing UEF MSc Computer Science study rights and Finland one-study-place-per-term rules can restrict enrolment.

records.field: Transport planning / demand analysis / urban mobility and transport policy

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: 2027 programme is listed, but formal 2027 guide sets coursework EBE deadline at 30 September 2026 and does not list MTransport as an exception: deadline has passed. Undated department page instead says 31 October, an unresolved conflict. Later consideration only if department permits and places remain; do not present October as a confirmed open 2027 deadline. Teaching timetable lists 2027 months, not all exact days.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: No reliable complete 2027 tuition total retrieved. Formal guide charges per enrolled course: SADC international students additionally pay International Administrative Fee; non-SADC coursework students also pay international faculty term fee. Rates, electives and individual fee category need a quote. Application: ZAR 100 South Africa/SADC; ZAR 300 outside SADC; UCT graduates normally exempt. International scholarships are limited partial awards, not full-cost funding.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: The programme-specific options page explicitly states that prior degrees need not be in a particular discipline. Standard route: university honours or four-year bachelor degree plus adequate numeracy and writing. A three-year bachelor/BTech alternative requires five years of relevant senior post-qualification experience and satisfactory marks, typically above 60%.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Transport planning / demand analysis / urban mobility and transport policy

sections.label: Language
sections.text: 2027 applicant guide: IELTS Academic 6.5, all bands 6.0; TOEFL iBT 88 (listening/writing 19, reading 20, speaking 22); PTE 67, communicative skills 59. Tests normally within two years. English-schooling exemptions have specified conditions. TOEFL/IELTS results due 12 January 2027. Programme-specific higher requirements were not found.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Numeracy: one semester of first-year university pure/applied mathematics or statistics, or Senior Certificate maths at least 50%; a numeracy test is possible otherwise. Foreign honours/three-year degree equivalence needs assessment. Programme publishes 190 credits: 60 core, 80 electives and two 25-credit projects. Normal coursework sequence spans two years. In addition to academic transcripts and applicable English evidence, the formal 2027 programme-specific checklist marks CV as required and portfolio, proposal, references and named supervisor as not required. Additional evidence can still be requested. Bridge and recognition: No automatic academic bridge is established. The five-year experience alternative is a substantive entry condition, not a short conversion course. Award structure: One MTransport endpoint. Other UCT Transport MPhil/MEng/MScEng awards are not counted in this batch. Scope caveats: Do not confuse this with engineering-only MEng/MScEng Transport options; those do not establish a maths conversion route. Do not automatically classify every three-year foreign honours degree as either accepted honours or the experience-required route. Equivalence is unassessed. The published 2027 guide outranks an undated recurring October instruction for planning purposes; late admission remains unconfirmed. No engineering-registration entitlement inferred from the professional master title. Housing application deadline of 31 July 2026 in the 2027 guide has also passed. Unassessed: citizenship, degree country/equivalence, transcript, GPA, language evidence, budget and intended intake are unknown.

records.title: Master of Information Science (MC-INFSCI), 18-month route
records.field: Libraries, archives, records management and digital preservation

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Published special-study-period application closings: 12 November 2026 (period 4), then 11 February, 6 May, 12 August and 11 November 2027. Periods broadly March–May, June–August, September–November and December–February. Exact teaching start and applicant-route availability require confirmation.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: 2026 domestic fee-paying first-year indicative tuition AUD 23,484 for 200 credits. This is neither an 18-month total nor a Commonwealth-supported quote. International course page says indicative fees unavailable. Later-year increases, admin/incidental fees, textbooks, fieldwork travel and full-degree total remain unverified. Generic scholarships directory is not evidence of a personal award; none budgeted.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Programme-specific entry requires at least a recognised three-year bachelor, without a subject or numerical grade restriction on the course page. Maths is plausibly within this screen; international equivalence remains assessed.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Libraries, archives, records management and digital preservation

sections.label: Language
sections.text: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall and 6.0 in each skill; approved alternatives available. English-medium study.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Competence with word processing and internet tools required. No compulsory professional experience or portfolio published. Two three-week fieldwork placements, one records/archives and one library/information setting, form part of the programme; placements are arranged for internal/external students. Work-based exemptions may be possible. No pre-master bridge required by the stated bachelor route. Duration and delivery: 18 months full-time or part-time equivalent, online, administered at Curtin Perth. Mid-year starters may face restricted full-time availability and extended duration. International page explicitly excludes Australian student-visa study. Overseas placement feasibility needs checking. The two-year extended option and interim diplomas are not additional counted endpoints. Award scope: Curtin University; Master of Information Science, MC-INFSCI. This is an information-professions qualification, not an Information Systems technology master. Professional recognition: Course reports that graduates in Australia may be eligible for ALIA associate membership, Australian Society of Archivists membership and RIMPA membership. These statements do not guarantee a legal licence, employment or recognition in every country. Verification caveats: International Australian student-visa restriction is explicit. Do not equate domestic annual fee to international or whole-degree cost. Placement requirements prevent treating online delivery as automatically location-independent. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no assumption about degree equivalence, grades, citizenship/residency, experience, English, budget, visa eligibility or admission.

sections.text: April 2027 direct master’s entry, second round. Specified eligibility inquiries/screening: November 6, 2026. sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Published 2027 charges: examination JPY 30,000 plus handling; entrance JPY 282,000; annual tuition JPY 535,800; two-year accident/liability insurance JPY 1,750–18,750. Calculated two-year tuition JPY 1,071,600; tuition+entrance+application+listed insurance JPY 1,385,350–1,402,350, before handling/living/travel and rate changes. No nationality/residency tuition surcharge is specified in this guide. Fees remain payable unless separately awarded funding. Scholarship option ADB–Japan Scholarship Program at GSID (April 2027): Deadline: June 30, 2026 extended deadline; EXPIRED. Conditions: ADB borrowing-country nationality; recognized bachelor; at least two full-time post-degree professional years; born on/after June 1, 1991; resident/working in home country; applicant income no more than USD 25,000/year and family USD 50,000/year. Prior graduate enrollment/study abroad normally excluded, with narrow home-country master/16-year-schooling exception. No ADB staff/close-family eligibility. Superior record, developed-country dual-citizenship prohibition, health and designated-institution staff restrictions additionally apply under provider rules. Must return/work at home at least two years; no ADB work for two years. Mandatory English test and competitive university/ADB selection. Coverage: Full tuition, National Health Insurance, monthly subsistence/housing for one person, books/miscellaneous and economy return airfare. JPY 147,000/month is explicitly a 2025 reference amount, not fixed 2027 funding. First year only initially; second-year continuation depends on satisfactory performance. Admissions/application fee coverage not explicitly itemized in the local call; do not assume every cost waived. Scholarship option MEXT embassy-recommended research-student pathway (2027 research-student entry, NOT direct 2027 MA): Deadline: GSID provisional-acceptance documents September 1, 2026; EXPIRED. Embassy first screening must already be passed; embassy deadline varies.. Conditions: Nondegree research-student enrollment first in April/October 2027; subsequent MA entrance exam needed for April 2028 degree entry. Earliest stated MA completion March 2030. University provisional acceptance does not guarantee MEXT scholarship. Kept separate from the two-year direct-entry endpoint. Coverage: Not costed as guaranteed MA funding; this is a longer conditional pathway. Published living components calculate to JPY91,500–121,000/month (rent JPY35,000–60,000; utilities JPY10,000; communication JPY1,500–6,000; food JPY45,000). Transport, books, supplies, National Health Insurance, deposits, flights, visa and other unspecified costs; this subtotal is not a complete living budget. Housing generally only 6–12 months in university residence; private accommodation needed afterward. University says prepare at least two months living funds.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: The 2027 regular master’s guide gives subject-unrestricted degree routes: accredited Japanese university; eligible statutory bachelor; 16 years formal education; or recognized overseas bachelor-equivalent from a program of at least three years. Final qualification due March 31, 2027. The statement of purpose explicitly anticipates changing academic major. This supports subject access for a mathematics graduate, not individual equivalence or admission.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Interdisciplinary development studies, public policy and international cooperation

sections.label: Language
sections.text: All GSID courses are taught in English. Required test minima: TOEFL iBT/Home 79 on 0–120 scale; Essentials 8.5; listed revised paper-delivered TOEFL 550; IELTS 6; Duolingo 110. Tests within two years before application opening. No exemption for native English or English-medium degree. ITP, TOEIC, IELTS Indicator, TOEFL MyBest and IELTS One Skill Retake not accepted. Interview may be Japanese or English; no compulsory JLPT found. Application language: Statement of purpose: Japanese up to 1,500 characters or English up to 600 words; proposal: Japanese up to 4,000 characters or English up to 1,600 words. Academic records/certificates require Japanese or English translations when needed. This does not make the degree Japanese-taught. Admission examination: Online oral examination may be in Japanese or English. JLPT evidence is optional in this guide; it is not a general entry requirement.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Regular AY2027 admission: no numerical GPA, mandatory subject-credit minimum or work-years minimum is specified. Chosen-field knowledge, logical thinking and research readiness are assessed. Category (6) foreign three-year-or-longer degree and category (8) minister-approved applicants must contact GSID by November 6, 2026; category (9) individual-equivalence applicants must submit the prescribed CV for screening by the same date and be at least 22 by end March 2027. Research proposal and statement of purpose required; recommendations/work evidence optional. Prior supervisor consent is not required. Accepted jobholders must later provide employer approval or a self-consent letter. Concurrent university enrollment is normally disallowed, with leave-of-absence and exceptional-permission qualifications. Degree-route details: (1) accredited Japanese university graduate, or completion by end March 2027; (2) statutory bachelor under School Education Law Article 104 paragraph 7(1), or award by end March 2027; (3) at least 16 years formal education in home country, or completion by end March 2027; (4) foreign correspondence education while in Japan meeting the guide’s 16-year qualification, or completion by end March 2027; English guide wording says up to 16 years, an awkward formulation not silently rewritten; (5) designated foreign-system university in Japan with at least 16 years formal education, or graduation by end March 2027; (6) recognized foreign bachelor-equivalent from an accredited/designated program of at least three years, including specified distance/foreign-system provision; degree by March 31, 2027; advance contact required; (7) minister-designated advanced vocational specialized/advanced-course qualification meeting the detailed statutory duration/continuity requirements; (8) minister approval under Ministry Notice No. 5 of 1953; advance contact required; (9) GSID individual qualification screening plus age at least 22 by end March 2027; advance screening required. Admissions-route linkage: The admissions page directly links the AY2027 second-round guide for the GSID master’s department; curriculum confirms English teaching. Japanese is an allowed dossier/oral-examination language, not evidence that this is a Japanese-taught route. Regular direct entry, ADB admission and MEXT research-student entry are different routes. The application checklist splits documents between email and post, both required. Duration and delivery: 2 years in principle; at least 30 Japanese credits plus supervised master’s thesis/examination. No ECTS equivalence is asserted. The separate one-year business-professionals route is not recruiting for 2027. Award scope: Nagoya University; Master of Arts in International Development (GSID). Five specialist education programs belong to this single award. Verification caveats: The general entry rule does not require a social-science bachelor, but selected specialization knowledge is assessed. No personal nationality, degree-country/length, grades, work history or language certificate assumed. No automatic full funding. Expired ADB and MEXT calls remain expired. 2027 admissions guide prohibits generative-AI-generated application documents; research here is information gathering, not application authoring. IELTS subtype detail is more explicit in the ADB call than regular guide; preserve route-specific language rules. Exact regular-guide TOEFL table wording is “The revised TOEFL Paper-delivered Test” with 550, whereas ADB prose calls 550 “PBT”; both are preserved as published, not silently normalized to a currently available test. Verify test-format acceptance before relying on this legacy-looking entry. Degree-route (4) has awkward English wording up to 16 years while other routes specify 16 years; retain this wording caveat and seek institutional interpretation if relying on that route. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no user citizenship, fee residency, degree/transcript/GPA, work experience, budget, language exemption, intake or individual admission/funding outcome inferred.

## 7. Boston University — LEAP into an engineering master's, USA
**Route:** Genuine engineering conversion pathway for non-engineering bachelor's graduates. Personalized undergraduate foundation phase, then master's in areas including electrical/computer engineering, mechanical engineering, robotics, biomedical engineering, materials or systems engineering. Potentially two or more years, depending on deficiencies.
**Background:** Four-year non-engineering bachelor's/equivalent; B or higher in STEM Calculus I before matriculation. GRE and English proficiency documentation listed by LEAP; check current application-specific requirements.
**Deadline:** Standing Fall deadlines January 15 and March 15; Spring November 1. 2027-specific label not confirmed.
**Cost/funding:** Master's phase 2026/27 USD2,282/credit: USD73,024 for a 32-credit degree, USD82,152 for 36 credits, PLUS foundation-phase tuition, fees/living. Foundation costs individualized and not quoted publicly on cost page. Merit scholarship consideration is competitive.
Sources: [eligibility/deadlines](https://www.bu.edu/eng/academics/explore-degree-programs/leap-a-masters-program-for-non-engineers/ [foundation pathway](https://www.bu.edu/academics/eng/programs/leap/ [tuition](https://www.bu.edu/eng/admissions/graduate/graduate-admissions/tuition-fees/ [scholarships](https://grad-programs.bu.edu/eng/leap/

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Main programme page labels its latest curriculum 2025/2026. No programme-specific open or next intake/deadline established as of 2026-10-01. The 2026/27 September advertisement lists other programmes and cannot supply this deadline.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Latest linked 2025/26 syllabus: local LKR 300,000 Master or LKR 375,000 entire MSc; foreign USD 2,000 Master or USD 2,500 entire MSc. Local totals are corroborated by January 2026 Expo price sheet. These are revisable published prices, not a future-intake quote. Add shared extra fees; no guaranteed funding. Additional charges: Current central fee table (LKR local/foreign): application 2,000/4,000; registration 5,000/10,000; refundable lending-library 2,000/4,000; reference-library 1,500/3,000; refundable science deposit 1,500/3,000; medical 500/1,000. Renewal after GPA release: stated LKR 2,000 per year until completion; foreign renewal treatment not separated. Programme fees are revisable. Living, travel and visa costs are additional/unpriced. Funding: No guaranteed tuition scholarship or personal funding eligibility established. Scholarship page lists merit awards; current handbook discusses budget-dependent support without a specific funded offer.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Programme curriculum accepts a bachelor degree or PGIS-accepted equivalent. This is a plausible mathematics/applied-mathematics route, subject to the shared 2026 institutional admission gate; personal acceptance is not established. General 2026 handbook section 6.5 sets alternative qualification routes in the relevant subject area: UGC-recognised BSc Honours/Special (SLQF 6), UGC-recognised BSc (SLQF 5), another PGIS-accepted equivalent with at least 30 relevant credits acceptable to the Board, OR the requirements stipulated in the particular Master/MSc programme. This is followed by required proficiency in an aptitude test, interview, or both. The BSc alternatives are not exhaustive; applicability, recognition and subject equivalence require PGIS assessment. Do not interpret the broader programme-specific wording as a personal admission guarantee.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Applied statistics, experimental design and data analysis

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English-medium; IELTS/TOEFL threshold and waiver rules unresolved.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Noncredit preliminary maths for applicants lacking calculus, sets and matrices; introductory statistics for those without basics. Preliminary programming is provided. No mandatory professional experience stated. No numeric undergraduate minimum identified for these coursework routes; programme GPA 3.00 is a completion/progression requirement, not a verified incoming GPA. Award and delivery: Selected Master: minimum/about 12 months, 30 coursework credits. MSc progression is separately conditional, minimum 24 months overall with full-time second-year research; see research_progression. Peradeniya-based; current programme-specific hybrid/contact timetable unresolved. Not verified fully online. Completion: Required coursework including five-credit independent study, at least C in each course and overall GPA at least 3.00. Research progression: Complete the required 30 coursework credits with GPA at least 3.00; satisfy programme requirements before upgrading registration. PGIS must approve the research title, place and supervisors. Submit the MSc research proposal form within two months of GPA release and obtain formal approval to commence. GPA eligibility does not establish an approved research placement, offer or personal progression decision. Master: 30 coursework credits including independent study, minimum 12 months. MSc: additional 30-credit research, minimum 24 months overall. Same work cannot earn both awards; do not count nested exits or research upgrades as extra independent options. The PGIS Scientific Writing Workshop is additionally required for award completion.

sections.label: Description
sections.text:
## 9. Simon Fraser — MSc Statistics or MSc Actuarial Science, Canada
**Route:** Two related standalone graduate options outside mathematics: statistical research/data work, or insurance/risk. Actuarial program includes a project and possible co-op; not merely professional-exam preparation. Still quantitative/theoretical, so confirm tolerance for statistical theory.
**Background:** Bachelor's and CGPA at least 3.0 plus strong references; advanced relevant statistics/actuarial coursework strengthens candidacy. No GRE; no supervisor needed before applying. English proficiency under SFU rules. Actuarial background may affect required course load; math bachelor's is relevant but not blanket readiness.
**2027 deadline:** January 7, 2027, opening October 1, 2026. Admissions page explicitly says Fall2027 but retains one stale “Fall2026 cohort” sentence; confirm if applying.
**Cost/funding:** International and domestic regular graduate tuition same: Fall2026 CAD2,192.57/term, approximately CAD6,577.71 for three terms, plus fees. sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Fall entry is recommended by MSHF criteria. General Daytona master's deadlines are recurring, undated rules: U.S. citizens July 1 for fall and November 1 for spring; international applicants June 1 for fall and October 1 for spring. These are not an expressly dated Fall 2027 MSHF announcement. The current 2026-27 calendar confirms fall classes began 24 August 2026 (historical) and spring classes begin 13 January 2027. As of the check date, the general international spring deadline falls today, but spring MSHF suitability/availability must be verified because the programme recommends fall. Fall 2027 class start unverified. The same general admissions page also describes typically February/fall and October/spring priority deadlines and rolling applications; these generic priority statements are distinct from the campus-specific deadline table and do not establish a dated MSHF intake.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: AY2026-27 Daytona tuition USD 1,912 per credit. At 36 credits, tuition-only arithmetic is USD 68,832 at unchanged rates; this is an illustration, not a fixed programme quote. Published annual campus fees are USD 1,926 for SGA/facilities/technology/health services. Application USD 50 non-refundable. Student insurance is charged unless an acceptable waiver is approved; only the preliminary AY2025-26 amount USD 1,982/year was shown, so current premium is a gap. Extra undergraduate prerequisites, lab/equipment charges, living, travel, visa, evaluation and future rate increases are excluded. The generic master's annual COA is USD 49,046 off-campus but covers only six credits per semester, not the nine-credit/semester MSHF plan. Full master's assistantships provide tuition waiver plus a stipend; require full graduate status, CGPA at least 3.0, adequate skills, at least six graduate credits, and typically 20 hours/week. Positions and application timing are departmental; no MSHF award amount, guaranteed availability or funding deadline verified. Daytona donor awards are variable, competitive, non-renewing automatically, for current students through the internal system; no new-entrant MSHF award entitlement established.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: The general admissions FAQ specifically identifies human factors as accepting varied undergraduate backgrounds. The 2026-27 Daytona MSHF criteria require knowledge of psychology and statistics, rather than a named bachelor's major, and allow assignment of undergraduate catch-up courses. This supports a plausible maths route, conditional on faculty assessment of preparation; statistics knowledge and psychology study cannot be assumed from a maths degree title.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Human factors, experimental psychology, cognitive engineering and ergonomics

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English instruction. For applicants whose primary language is not English, 2026-27 catalog minima include IELTS 6.0; TOEFL iBT 79 if taken before 21 January 2026 or 4 on the revised scale on/after that date; Duolingo 105; PTE Academic 59. Other listed tests: TOEFL Essentials 8.5, Cambridge 170, EIKEN Pre-1, LanguageCert Academic 65. Six postsecondary English Composition credits at C or above can evidence proficiency. Successful ERLI study plus director recommendation may permit an exam exemption; ERLI admission does not guarantee degree admission. No exemption is assumed.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Accredited baccalaureate and Daytona CGPA 3.0/4.0. Programme criteria describe 3.0 as the usual evidence of a strong record. Psychology and statistics prerequisite knowledge is required; no quantified credits, named cognition class, prior laboratory experience, programming, creative portfolio or minimum professional employment duration is specified in the inspected MSHF criteria. GMAT/GRE not required. Undergraduate prerequisites may be assigned; their credit count, completion timing and cost are individualized and not established. General conditional admission is discretionary, not a guaranteed bridge: the initial nine graduate credits require B or better in each course and CGPA 3.0. Standard supporting-document guidance discusses statement of objectives, resume, and academic/professional references; the public MSHF criteria do not give an unambiguous reference count. The campus landing page refers to three letters, so the exact MSHF checklist remains a verification gap. Foreign educational experience normally requires an official course-by-course evaluation in English including GPA and U.S. equivalence, with applicant-paid evaluation/translation costs. Duration and delivery: Daytona Beach in-person, 36 credits. Both thesis and non-thesis options count as this same endpoint. The current catalog supplies two-year plans with four fall/spring semesters at nine credits each; the department also describes the conventional master's as four semesters. A separate Worldwide online delivery exists with a different 30/33-credit structure; it is not counted as another endpoint here and its fees/admission rules are not substituted for Daytona rules. Award scope: Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Human Factors and Behavioral Neurobiology; Daytona Beach, Florida. Professional-recognition scope: The 2026-27 catalog identifies the Daytona MS as HFES-accredited. This is programme recognition; academic admission and completion do not automatically confer an engineering licence, psychology licence, professional certification, immigration permission or employment eligibility. Verification caveats: Do not import the 2.5 Worldwide GPA, online tuition, online credit count or faster generic duration into the Daytona endpoint. Do not apply the ERAU fast-track any-bachelor/3.5 rule to an external applicant; that is a distinct internal pathway, not the ordinary route. The undergraduate catch-up allowance is explicit, but the university has not specified this applicant's bridge. The programme-specific no-GRE policy controls over general pages saying tests are required for some degrees. No official dated Fall 2027 MSHF admissions or funding deadline found; recurring deadlines retained with that limitation. The standard first-nine-graduate-credit conditional-performance rule is separate from assigned undergraduate prerequisites; custom conditional offers can impose individual terms. No automatic bridge, timing, visa availability or 2027 curriculum promise is inferred. Personal eligibility: Unassessed. No assumptions about transcript, grades, degree equivalence, citizenship/residency, immigration status, work, English exemption, budget or selection.

sections.label: Description
sections.text:
## 8. Tilburg University, Netherlands — MSc Business Analytics and Operations Research
- Fit: English, one year, optimization/data-informed business decisions. Econometrics/OR or similar degree required, with strong math/probability. Math graduate is a case-by-case related-discipline candidate; a pre-master of up to 36 ECTS can remedy deficiencies. GRE Q160 required unless relevant partner-university exemption; IELTS 6.5 overall with writing/speaking 6.0 or another accepted proof.
- Intake: Page explicitly discusses February and September 2027. Current deadlines for non-EEA nationals: 1 October for late-January start and 1 April for late-August start; EEA: 1 December/1 June. Dutch residence permit can change applicable deadline. February 2027 non-EEA deadline is therefore imminent, 1 October 2026; don't pressure an unprepared application.
- Cost/funding: Exact 2027 tuition and program scholarship offer not verified. Non-Dutch-degree application fee €100 from September 2027 onward; scholarship deadlines can precede admission deadlines.

## Two Middle East alternatives

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: The fee regulation published 31 March 2026 specifies EUR2,225 per semester in 2027/28 and EUR2,350 in 2028/29 under M-PO-Pub-2026. Calculated four-semester tuition for October-2027 entry is EUR9,150, assuming completion over those academic years and unchanged rules. No nationality fee split is stated. The programme page quotes a current semester contribution of EUR340 and initial student card EUR20; these are planning figures, and contributions may change. Four semesters at that contribution would add EUR1,380, giving EUR10,530 institutional tuition/contribution/card charges only. Tuition continues beyond normal duration; excursions can cost extra. Application fee and other individual charges were not independently established. No personal affordability or scholarship outcome is asserted. Living-cost scope: The current financing page quotes EUR992/month; its linked 2026–28 budget identifies this as a January-2025 baseline including rent, health insurance, food and personal items. The university’s approximately EUR31,500 total is for its 2026–28, 22-month illustration, excluding travel home; it is not a 2027-entry quote. Actual housing, insurance, travel, visa/residence costs and deposits require an individual updated budget. Funding: Helmut-Schmidt is a separate competitive route whose 2027 application period has ended. Its specified first-degree fields are social/political sciences, law, economics, public policy/administration; mathematics-only funding eligibility is not established. It also has upper-third grades, relevant experience, country/residence and degree-recency gates. Ordinary other-discipline admission does not establish scholarship eligibility. This record is justified by ordinary subject accessibility and published self-funded fees, not assumed scholarship support.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Ordinary admission expressly invites applicants whose undergraduate degree is outside the preferred social-science, economics and law fields, provided their motivation explains policy relevance and analytical preparation. This supports a plausible mathematics-to-public-policy route; it does not establish individual eligibility. General rules require a completed qualifying higher-education degree with a standard duration of at least six semesters.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Interdisciplinary public policy, public administration, policy analysis and governance

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English-taught. IELTS Academic minimum 6.5 overall and every component; TOEFL iBT minimum 4.5 overall and every component for tests from 21 January 2026, or 90 overall for earlier tests; Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency also listed. Apply the controlling rule’s maximum two-year test age; the website explicitly mentions this for IELTS/TOEFL. Official proof of an English-medium degree can replace a test. No personal language exemption assumed. German is not required for admission; students without A2 German must take the curriculum’s German-language module.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: The controlling 2026 MPP rules require at least German grade “good”, or proven top-25% cohort performance (German law state-exam alternative: at least 7.50 points). The examination committee determines foreign-degree equivalence. They require at least one year in a directly policy-related or indirectly policy-related, analytically demanding occupation. The admissions page additionally asks for above-average professional performance. Work documentation is mandatory at application; internships/voluntary work may count, subject to assessment. Analytical aptitude, policy interest, CV and statement of purpose are assessed. No prior subject-credit quota or compulsory pre-master bridge was identified. Duration and delivery: Two years/four semesters, 120 ECTS, full-time in Erfurt; winter entry. Includes professional practice, capstone work and thesis. Specialisations are choices within one MPP, not separate programme endpoints. Award scope: University of Erfurt; Master of Public Policy (M.P.P.). Verification caveats: Grade and work requirements use the binding German 2026 rules; the public-facing work wording is softer, so do not infer that unrelated work or no experience is sufficient. Work may combine placements totaling a year; the university must assess relevance and equivalence. No user experience, grades, degree status, citizenship, visa status, language proof or intended intake is inferred. All final degree documents are required before final admission; certified or digitally verifiable records and translations may be needed. The 2026-entry tuition calculation remains EUR8,650; do not carry it over to October-2027 entry. An ordinary admission route may be included independently of narrower scholarship eligibility; published tuition is not a total-cost or affordability guarantee. The separate university winter-2026/27 contribution table quotes EUR357.80 including a EUR20 card for undergraduate/consecutive master programmes; it does not expressly list this continuing-education MPP. Do not silently apply that category. Use the MPP page’s quoted contribution as an indicative figure; the actual MPP semester invoice and future 2027/28 contributions remain unverified. The MPP page quotes EUR340 plus EUR20 card, while the central 2026/27 table gives EUR357.80 including card for undergraduate/consecutive-master categories. The continuing-education MPP category is not automatically equivalent; its quoted contribution remains indicative and no 2027/28 contribution invoice is verified. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no user citizenship, fee residency, degree/transcript/GPA, work experience, budget, language exemption, intake or individual admission/funding outcome inferred.

sections.text: 2026/27 application fee EUR 30. The formal 2026/27 notice expressly accepts foreign university degrees subject to university recognition; an awkward webpage sentence about providing an Italian qualification should not be read as a blanket foreign-degree exclusion.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Fall 2027 cohort is advertised open; closes 8 January 2027. The exact opening day and teaching start day are unverified. Admissions page is current; the requirements page still contains a stale Fall 2026 timeline.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: MDM admissions close | 2027-01-08 | All MDM applicants; SFU-administered application | reviewed_source_date

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: 2026–27 published tuition: CAD 38,338.59 domestic or 69,709.80 international. Published tuition-plus-fee totals: CAD 42,594.48 / 74,246.69. These totals include a refundable CAD 1,500 equipment deposit. Application fee: CAD 120 Canadian-transcript / 160 international-transcript applicants. These are not Fall 2027 quotes; living costs extra. Domestic table arithmetic is inconsistent: term tuition sums CAD 38,338.14 and term grand totals sum CAD 42,594.03, each CAD 0.45 below the published headline. Keep both as disputed source values. Optional fifth-term published charge CAD 604.30 (318.36 tuition plus 285.94 fees), subject to revision. Applicable international BC Medical Services Plan charge CAD 75/month is additional; the first-term university insurance charge must not be added again to the CDM total. Conditional Technical Communication Bundle is separately priced; its published fee totals are internally inconsistent and no bundle cost is added automatically. Living, travel, materials and conditional extra courses remain outside a verified all-in total. Competitive funding: New applicants are generally automatically considered for competitive scholarships; the CDM Scholarship has variable value. Pat Hibbitts is an exception requiring a separate application. Technology support up to CAD 2,000 has full-time and CGPA 3.5 conditions; no personal award or net price assumed.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Programme explicitly permits unrelated-degree applicants to argue their disciplinary connection and benefit. Normally requires a four-year undergraduate degree or equivalent acceptable to all four partners, plus B+ (76%) in third/fourth-year courses. This is a conditional cross-disciplinary route, not explicit maths acceptance.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Digital product and experience design / creative technology / interdisciplinary project leadership

sections.label: Language
sections.text: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall/6.0 each; TOEFL iBT 4.5 overall/4.0 each, or pre-21-January-2026 tests 90/no section below 20. Results valid two years. Degree-based exemption has country and English-medium conditions. Meeting minimum scores does not ensure committee approval.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Demonstrated computing ability and familiarity with digital-media tools are mandatory; no named software or coding language is prescribed. Work samples/portfolio, a 250–500-word explanation, 30–45-second introduction video, letter of intent (maximum 750 words), CV, 3–5 references and transcripts are required. Shortlisted applicants interview. No universal employment-duration minimum is stated. SFU Fall 2026 calendar also publishes cumulative GPA 3.0 on the Canadian scale/equivalent, alongside B+ (76%) in the last two undergraduate years; conditional/alternative admission is discretionary and may require additional first-year courses. Calendar related-discipline wording and website unrelated-discipline case must be read together. Mandatory application-system programme survey also required; calendar states three reference letters while the admissions page requests three to five. Duration and delivery: Normally 16 months/four terms, 51 units, full-time in Vancouver. Required six-unit fourth-term DMED 530 Internship is a career-exploration course; it is not an actual internship placement. Work, co-op, internships or professional development may be pursued; employment placement is not guaranteed. A fifth term is possible for an eight-month Internship course. Award scope: One MDM, administered through SFU, bearing all four partner institutions’ seals. Neither partners nor internship are separate endpoints. Preparation/recognition: A Technical Communication Bundle may be offered conditionally for English preparation; it is not an automatic academic bridge from a maths degree and is not separately counted. No regulated professional licence is established. Verification caveats: Admission remains competitive even when minima are met. Fee schedule is dated 2026–27, with last-update notation November 2025; do not roll it forward. Old FAQ English thresholds and former Pre-MDM language pathway are superseded by the current admissions requirements page. The course named Internship is career exploration, not a promised employment placement; do not turn the title into a universal placement requirement. Personal eligibility: Personal eligibility remains unassessed: degree length/country/equivalence, grades, creative or computing work, employment, citizenship, English evidence, budget and intended intake are unknown.

sections.label: Description
sections.text:
### 10. KAUST, Saudi Arabia — MS Statistics
- Application-oriented statistical data science, biostatistics, environment, computation and time series. English. General admission requires a relevant bachelor's and GPA at least 3.0/4.0; mathematics-to-statistics fit needs department confirmation/transcript assessment because no current explicit list naming mathematics as a guaranteed qualifying degree was retrieved. Treat as a promising research-fit option, not verified direct eligibility.
- Confirmed fall-2027 window: opened 28 September 2026; round-2 deadline 3 January 2027; decisions 14 February; start 29 August. Dates marked tentative. Spring 2027 is PhD-only.
- Funding: All admitted master's students receive KAUST Fellowship covering tuition, housing, health insurance, relocation and more, except some externally sponsored/funded students may be ineligible. Program normally 36 credits over three semesters plus summer; thesis option.
- Sources: [Statistics](https://stat.kaust.edu.sa/study/prospective-students [entry requirements](https://admissions.kaust.edu.sa/how-to-apply/entry-requirements [2027 timeline](https://admissions.kaust.edu.sa/how-to-apply/admission-timelines [master/funding](https://admissions.kaust.edu.sa/study/master's-degree

## Exclusion and practical interpretation
- Do not recommend Potsdam MSc Data Science as currently open: applications and enrollment are suspended from winter2026/27. [Official status](https://www.uni-potsdam.de/en/mnfakul/study-and-teaching/master/data-science
- Best explicit mathematics-degree pathways in this list: Mannheim Data Science, ETH Data Science, Paris-Saclay DKAI and MBZUAI AI. Each still has selection/prerequisites.
- Potential bridge route: Tilburg BAOR pre-master, subject to assessment.
- Heaviest pre-existing CS gate: Saarland DSAI; it should not be sold as a conversion degree.
- Strongest verified institutional full-funding route here: KAUST; eligibility/research fit still to confirm. Low tuition is not full funding: living expenses remain material in Germany, France and Switzerland.

sections.text: Ergonomics, human-centred systems, usability and user research

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English-medium online teaching. Programme page specifies IELTS 6.5 overall and 6.5 in each component, or listed alternatives. Do not assume an English-medium prior degree exempts the user. sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: No fixed psychology/cognition credits, laboratory experience, creative portfolio or required years of work appear in the listed degree-entry gate. Workplace application is encouraged in teaching; access to a suitable context for assessments/research should be checked individually. Three staged awards permit PGCert/PGDip progression to MSc; these are award stages, not a promised remedial bridge or separate endpoints. Standalone modules exist, but taking one before MSc enrolment can affect CIEHF recognition. [D1] Duration and delivery: Three years part-time online, 180 UK credits. Standard sequence starts September; year 1 fundamentals/cognitive psychology/physical ergonomics, year 2 investigation/systems/option, year 3 60-credit research project. Approximately 20 hours weekly. [D1,D2] Award scope: University of Derby, online provision. One MSc endpoint: general, Healthcare and Behaviour Change option-based named awards are grouped; no separate counts for PGCert, PGDip, standalone modules or pathways. [D1,D2] Professional-recognition scope: CIEHF qualifying course permits graduates to apply for Graduate Membership; chartered/registered standing needs a separate process. Required module order matters. No clinical/psychologist licence or engineering licence follows automatically. [D1,D2; scope limitation] Verification caveats: Unrestricted degree wording is an inference-based subject fit, not explicit all-disciplines acceptance. Do not infer January or May entry from general online calendars. Do not treat GBP 9,720 at 2026/27 rates as a guaranteed three-year payable total. No assumption that the user has workplace access, relevant experience, English exemption or loan eligibility. Online delivery does not itself establish UK visa sponsorship or permission to relocate; no personal immigration eligibility is assessed. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no assumption about transcript, grades, degree equivalence, citizenship, fee status, work experience, budget, English exemption, visa or intended intake.

facts: Replace unresolved English completion with sufficient English courses to satisfy graduation requirements. IMIS has green markers for both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 in the official prospectus; actual semester offerings remain controlling. This is not the fully-English red designation.

Do not substitute the currently open September 23–October 13 INTENSE window for IMIS general admission. The actual Spring 2027 INTENSE prospectus lists only Engineering Science, Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Electrical Engineering, all Chinese-taught. An indexed IMIS portal-detail page under an INTENSE heading is insufficient evidence of participation.
General Spring 2027 application period was July 1–September 15, 2026; closed. February 2027 is the stated semester start. No general Fall 2027 window was published on the checked schedule.

Official prospectus lists the IMIS master’s in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027, with one master’s place in the AY 2026/27 quota table. It requires a bachelor’s, CEFR B1 English evidence for non-English-speaking applicants (waiver/alternative rules apply), autobiography, study plan and interview. No mathematics-specific admission acceptance is stated.

NCKU eligibility follows MOE international-student rules, including no previous Overseas Chinese study/current-year placement. Dual or former ROC citizenship, Hong Kong/Macao permanent residency and former Mainland Chinese status require individual residence/household-registration checks. Qualifying former Mainland Chinese foreign nationals can use the international route after six continuous overseas years; do not treat all such applicants as automatically excluded.

Foreign degrees require recognition under the applicable Taiwan rules; credentials from Mainland China and Hong Kong/Macao follow separate recognition provisions. Admission-route eligibility is not the same as recognition of the degree.

Fall 2027 general dates and intake-specific quotas, exact current tuition, and mathematics-background acceptance remain unverified. The general application remains closed, and the current INTENSE prospectus does not supply an alternative IMIS intake.
Individual nationality/residence eligibility, degree recognition and English-waiver evidence remain unresolved without the applicant’s details.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: For 2027 PGDip admission, applications run 17 August–9 October 2026. The current 2027 MInf window is 1 September–20 November 2026 for applicants who can meet MInf entry requirements for that cycle. Starting the PGDip in 2027 cannot supply that qualification for immediate 2027 MInf entry. A later separate MInf application, qualifying grades, research fit and supervisor-capacity selection are required; the later cycle is unverified.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: 2026 subject-band planning estimate: PGDip R30,740; MInf R19,650–20,090 per registered year, exact programme band unresolved. Tuition formula R30,740 + n×(R19,650–20,090); a hypothetical 1+2-year scenario is R70,040–70,920, not a typical duration or 2027 quote. PGDip foreign-address levy is R3,905 per annual module for Africa or R7,470 for rest of world; six modules imply R23,430/R44,820 at unchanged rates. MInf rest-of-world levy is R12,640 per registration year. R160 once-off formal-student-number application fee where applicable. Books, IT, SAQA, practical/research/travel, repeats and future increases excluded. No applicant fee class or funding award assumed.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Programme-specific conversion purpose plus compulsory-module descriptions explicitly target bachelor's graduates in any non-Information-Science field. The endpoint accepts an appropriate Information Science PGDip. This supports a mathematics-to-LIS conversion route, not an individual eligibility guarantee. Overseas practical access and residence clearance remain separate unresolved feasibility gates.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Library and information science / information management / digital curation

sections.label: Language
sections.text: All six published PGDip modules are in English. The MInf department supports language-proficiency testing for foreign students; no numerical MInf test threshold or personal exemption verified. Research language must be formally agreed at the start under UNISA procedures, with supervision/examination capacity for any approved alternative.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Appropriate accredited NQF7 qualification; at least 60% in major(s) or a selected set of NQF7 modules. Foreign qualification evaluation required. No standard work-experience minimum stated on this specific admission page. Master: Appropriate honours/PGDip, or 480-credit bachelor with at least 96 NQF8 credits in Information Science; average 60%. Applicants admitted using a PGDip/qualifying 480-credit bachelor who lack research methodology may have to complete HIN4801 at NQF8 for non-degree purposes before dissertation registration. No automatic extra module is assumed for successful graduates of the published 90003 curriculum. Transcript and intended-research document; departmental 2–5-page LIS outline; viable topic aligned with expertise and available supervision. Separate master's application and selection. AIS4803 requires a practical portfolio in a LIS environment. Actual overseas library/practical access and foreign-residence clearance remain unresolved. General 2026 Student Rules permit practical examinations to be limited to South Africa; whether AIS4803 has such an examination is unestablished. Confirm current assessment instructions and programme-specific access before relying on worldwide remote completion.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Current rules require an academic university bachelor and outstanding quantitative/research preparation, without naming a closed subject list. FAQ discusses applicants from quantitative programmes gaining micro/macro preparation. This supports a conditional maths-to-economics route, not an unrestricted any-degree assertion. Completed academic university bachelor is required by the 2026–27 AER Article 3.1; foreign level is assessed using Nuffic guidance. The admissions webpage also mentions bachelor and/or master; do not interpret it as waiving the bachelor rule. A 2027–28 AER has not been verified.

sections.label: Field

sections.label: Language

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: No fixed admission ECTS distribution verified. Initial micro/macro coursework advised for quantitative entrants; advanced-econometrics option needs stronger prior econometrics. Outstanding academic performance and research potential; no universal numeric GPA minimum published in current requirements. Applicants without a Dutch degree by programme start need all three GRE General sections; quantitative below 160 is rejected, while top-decile quantitative performance is typical rather than a second formal cutoff. Two academic references and PhD-oriented motivation required. Current webpage includes interview; 2026–27 AER says interview may form part of selection. Experience: Research potential assessed. Research internships/publications are helpful, not mandatory extracurricular requirements; required paid-work duration not verified. Award identity: One jointly offered MSc in Economics, CROHO 65027, by Erasmus University Rotterdam, University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. EUR is the primary enrolment/administration institution; registration at three partners is not three awards. Delivery: Two years, 120 EC, full-time only. English instruction across Amsterdam and Rotterdam; the 2026–27 AER normally requires physical lecture attendance. Research training for a PhD, with no guaranteed PhD appointment. Personal eligibility remains unassessed. Genuine PhD ambition is required; no PhD appointment is guaranteed. Scholarship renewal GPA thresholds are not admission GPA requirements.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: 2027 application closed 21 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST. Existing applicants may have authorised degree/test extensions to 11 December 2026; that is not a reopening. Next advertised scholarship intake September 2028; no 2028 application deadline yet published.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Funding rules cover 2025–2028 intakes. EUR 18,000 participation charge covered by EMJM or a separate tuition-fee scholarship for all selected students; insurance included. Competitive EMJM allowance EUR 1,400/month, maximum EUR 33,600/24 months. Other living, travel, visa and document costs remain; pre-arrival expenses must be financed upfront and are not reimbursed. Scholarship conditions: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (Rules 2025–2028; next available application intake announced September 2028): Full-time; no previous EMJM award; first payment after arrival in Krems, SEPA bank account required; residence/mobility constraints apply. EU nationality balance applies; cohort-specific quota not retrieved.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Any subject accepted. First university degree must itself represent at least three full-time years/180 ECTS and qualify for postgraduate study. Combining shorter bachelor and later degrees, or using work experience, cannot satisfy that first-degree minimum.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Higher-education governance, policy and innovation management

sections.label: Language
sections.text: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall/5.5 bands; TOEFL iBT before 21 January 2026: 92/20 sections; on/after: 4.5/4 sections; PTE62 or listed Cambridge tests. Exemptions limited to qualifying exclusively English studies and specified countries/campuses; English-medium study elsewhere is insufficient.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Two years/120 ECTS, full-time on-site. Relevant motivation required; work experience advantageous, not mandatory. Application includes essay, motivation letter, CV, two references; shortlisted applicants submit video. No design portfolio specified. Mobility and residence: Austria then Finland; semester 3 includes Asian (China/India) and European specialisation, followed by thesis at a specialisation host and compulsory eight-week internship. Consortium decides allocation. Two 30-ECTS countries must differ from residence at enrolment; Austrian/Finnish residents cannot choose UWK/TAU specialisation. Award structure: Institutional Research or Research Management/Digital Transformation: TAU+UWK joint Master of Administrative Sciences. Leadership/Management: UASO+UWK joint MSc; Learning/Teaching: ELTE+UWK joint MSc. Sustainability Education/Social Entrepreneurship: TIET MA Sustainability Education + UWK MSc (Continuing Education). Educational Planning/Development: BNU MA Education + UWK MSc (Continuing Education). Policy Analysis: Aveiro Master in Administration and Public Policies + UWK MSc (Continuing Education) + TAU Master of Administrative Sciences. Scope caveats: Track-dependent degrees remain explicitly distinct below; one centrally admitted MARIHE programme is counted, not seven university listings. No guaranteed living-cost coverage or EMJM award. Separate two-per-intake travel/visa grants up to EUR 6,000 for eligible disadvantaged/first-in-family non-EMJM students are not general scholarships for everyone; no personal eligibility inferred. Non-EU/EEA participants require relevant residence permissions; non-EMJM participants must show sufficient funds. Current immigration figures are not projected into 2028.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: 2026/2028 advertised cohort; deadline 10 January 2026. Departmental page expressly says registration closed for 2026. No 2027/next-round date verified.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: 2026/2028 advert: LKR 650,000 course fee. Department page says this includes LKR 5,000 registration and LKR 5,000 library fee; additional LKR 5,000 refundable library deposit. This LKR quote is not verified for foreign applicants; international fee, application fee and funding remain unverified. Erasmus+ curriculum collaboration does not establish a student scholarship.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Recognised bachelor including 30 credits in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related discipline; alternatively a recognised relevant SLQF level 6-or-above qualification. Mathematics is explicitly named; the user’s actual credits and overseas qualification recognition remain unassessed.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Data science / artificial intelligence / applied statistics

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English is explicitly stated in the directly retrieved official FGS handbook effective 1 October 2025, printed p.158, served from the September 2026 upload linked by the current FGS Downloads page. Numerical English-test threshold and waiver rules remain unverified.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: No numerical incoming admission GPA or work-experience minimum stated in the departmental/handbook criteria. The current official handbook, directly fetched from the live FGS Downloads link on 1 October 2026, requires an aptitude test if needed and an interview for shortlisted applicants based on test performance (printed p.158). Award and delivery: Two years/four semesters, with coursework and an annual 18-credit research project in year two; optional taught modules continue into year two. The 2026 advert simplifies this as first-year coursework and second-year research. Physical weekend sessions Saturday/Sunday 08:00–17:00 at the university, Faculty of Applied Sciences, Gangodawila, Nugegoda. Bring-your-own-laptop approach in the dated advert. Not verified as fully remote or visa-supporting. Completion and progression: Selected MSc (SLQF 10): handbook printed pp.162/165 requires GPA at least 2.70 over 42 taught credits at the end of semester four and grade B or higher in the annual 18-credit Research Project. These are graduation criteria, not an undergraduate admission GPA or a verified year-one research-progression threshold. The latter remains unverified; do not infer automatic research progression. Uncounted Master of Data Science and AI exit (SLQF 9) requires 30 credits, GPA at least 2.70 at end of semester two and at least B− in the five-credit Independent Study (p.162). No separate sibling fee or guaranteed later transfer is established.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: 2026-entry regular/non-NRI tuition: INR 150,000 per semester in 2026/27 and 158,000 in 2027/28, totaling INR 616,000. Calculated academic cash outlay INR 684,600 includes published fees, INR 12,600 refundable security and INR 6,200 PG alumni fee; housing/materials extra. Delhi NRI-category tuition alone: INR 907,000 + 952,000 = 1,859,000. Fee category/revisions require confirmation. Regular total arithmetic: (150,000 x 2 + 158,000 x 2) tuition + 20,500 library + 10,000 mediclaim/student development + 10,000 exam + 9,300 registration + 12,600 refundable security + 6,200 alumni = INR 684,600. NRI Delhi published annual grand totals INR 1,019,900 and 1,047,500 sum to INR 2,067,400, including fees/security/registration but before a possible INR 6,200 PG alumni charge: footnote applicability to NRI needs confirmation. These are 2026-entry schedules, revisable, not 2027-entry quotes. Application fee extra: regular Open/OBC-NCL/Open-EWS INR 2,000; SC/ST/PwD INR 500; foreign/NRI/OCI/PIO/SAARC route INR 11,100. Test, materials, housing, travel and other living costs extra; fee category unassessed. Competitive funding: SARTHAK is conditional financial assistance for regular students meeting scheme criteria. The reviewed prospectus establishes its existence, not a personal award, guaranteed percentage or new-entrant 2027 deadline. UDAAN concerns foreign-study opportunities and is not assumed to fund the degree itself.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Verified call only 2026/27: closed 8 January 2026, 11:00 CET; programme started 14 September 2026. Graduation deadline was 24 July 2026; Environmental Finance applicants with Chinese/Indian/Vietnamese degrees needed APS by 15 July. No 2027 call or scholarship quota verified.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: 2026/27 notice: maximum 14 competitive full EMJM awards, EUR 1,400/month for actual programme period, covering travel/visa/installation/subsistence; scholarship page covers participation costs. sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: 2026/27 notice explicitly accepts mathematics bachelor degrees. Three-year first-cycle degree or suitable foreign qualification required; foreign award must permit second-cycle access and pass recognition/authenticity checks.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Energy transition, environmental finance and energy economics

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English minimum CEFR B2, evidenced through a certificate on the programme accepted list. Listed online tests are not accepted; certificate validity is two years relative to call deadline. Recheck the test list for any later intake. Published 2026 accepted-test table maps IELTS 5.5–6.5 (Academic or General Training), TOEFL iBT 80–99, and PTE Academic 59–75 to B2; no new TOEFL-scale conversion inferred.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: 24 months/120 ECTS. Mandatory in-person GRE taken within two years, transcript/ISCED mapping and CV. Admission score at least 60/100; scholarship interview for scores at least 80, attendance required. No quantified work minimum or portfolio stated. Mobility and residence: Mandatory track-specific physical mobility. Official 2026/27 notice: Renewable Technologies semesters 1–4 London (Dauphine), Bologna, Bologna, Munich research/internship; Environmental Finance Munich, Munich, Paris, Bologna research/internship; Climate&Business Bologna, Munich, Paris, Paris research/internship. General mobility page allows fourth-semester partner/company placements; confirm assigned thesis location. Residence-sensitive EMJM two-country/30-ECTS rule and visas require individual review. Award structure: Multiple degree: Bologna Master in Greening Energy Market and Finance; LMU Master in Financial and Insurance Mathematics; Paris Dauphine Master in Economics and Finance. Scope caveats: Three tracks are Renewable Technologies, Environmental Finance and Climate&Business; applicants choose one. Count the integrated EMJM once, with three named diplomas, not three extra endpoints. Do not substitute Bologna standalone GrEnFIn or an older double-degree selection for this consortium EMJM admission/funding route.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Published September 2027 course is 18 months full-time in Suzhou, with dissertation. No mandatory work years or portfolio for standard degree entry; non-standard experience route is discretionary. Application includes personal statement (at most 800 words), transcripts with grading scale, degree evidence, English evidence, category-specific ID/passport and two academic referees’ contact details; certified English translations accompany non-English originals. Individual selection remains competitive. Bridge and recognition: No compulsory academic conversion year published. sections.text: University admissions explicitly name mathematics among accepted bachelor's subjects. The qualifying German or equivalent foreign degree must comprise at least 180 credits. sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Admission is competitive: undergraduate grades contribute up to 60 selection points and a shortlisted online interview up to 40. Modules cover perception/attention/action, memory/emotion/language/consciousness, neurocognitive methods, probabilistic/statistical modelling, programming, laboratory and research practice, plus thesis and oral examination.

Foreign-national admission is subject to nationality, ROC citizenship/household-registration history, overseas residence and Overseas Chinese status rules. sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: University minimum baccalaureate GPA 3.0/4.0 and recognized U.S. degree or international equivalent. The programme requires six undergraduate psychology credits including statistics and research methods. Transcripts, 2-4-page goals statement, resume and two references are required by programme sources. The statement asks about preparation/career goals and two or three possible faculty mentors. GRE optional. No mandatory creative portfolio, programming, laboratory hours, specified prior cognitive-psychology course or fixed work-experience duration found in the inspected checklist. Psychology provisional admits must earn 3.25 GPA over 12 psychology credits; this is discretionary rather than an advertised automatic conversion year. University policy prohibits provisional and conditional admission for F-1/J-1 students, so those applicants cannot assume they can arrive and bridge later. Foreign transcripts require translation where applicable and equivalency evaluation; Mason's internal evaluation is free, with submission six weeks early advised; outside evaluations can cost extra. Duration and delivery: In-person at Fairfax, usually 1.5-2 years; typically full-time, with part-time consideration for flexible schedules. Courses mainly weekday daytime and the degree cannot be completed fully online. One endpoint only: optional thesis/practicum are not separate awards. The authoritative 2026-27 catalog HF curriculum specifies 30 credits and is the controlling academic evidence. Departmental overview pages instead say 32 credits; this is an unresolved source contradiction, not an interchangeable 30/32-credit study choice. Confirm the applicable catalog and individualized degree audit before planning a binding total. Thesis and practicum each require permission. It is not the department's clinical PhD route and does not establish eligibility for clinical psychologist licensure or automatic professional registration. Occupational titles listed in marketing are not licensing promises. sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Fall entry; published recurring priority deadline 5 January has no explicit year. Do not label it a confirmed 2027 deadline or an open 2027 call. Later review only if places remain. The programme page still advertises its Fall 2026 online launch.

sections.text: 2026/27 tuition USD 2,182 per credit. At an unchanged rate, 36 credits would be USD 78,552 tuition (calculation, not a two-year quote). Annual increases, mandatory university/health fees, applicable international fees, insurance and living costs are additional; 2027/28 rate unverified. Published 2026/27 charges: University Services USD 720 per fall/spring semester (including Student Health Services), Student Senate USD 9 per semester, Orientation USD 177 once, and NYC F-1/J-1 international-services fee USD 113 per semester where applicable. Annual student health insurance USD 4,859 (fall 1,970; spring 2,889), including online-only degree students, may be waived with qualifying comparable coverage. Do not add a separate health-services fee. Application fee unresolved: admissions page states USD 50 domestic/international transfer or 75 first-year international, while the 2026/27 fee schedule states USD 54 domestic/97 international. Delivery, applicant category, future-year increases and insurance waiver require confirmation; no all-in two-year total asserted. Separate 2026/27 NYC academic-year living estimates: books/supplies USD 1,450, personal 1,540, housing/food 27,400 on campus or 29,310 off campus or 14,655 with family, plus transport 1,360 on/off campus or 3,510 with family. Estimates are not bills or guaranteed twelve-month budgets; do not double-add housing/meal-plan charges, and do not apply NYC living figures to online learners elsewhere. Competitive funding: Admitted students automatically receive merit-scholarship consideration based on application strength. Amount is not guaranteed; international applicants are eligible for merit awards. January priority deadline is also relevant to competitive funding, but its cycle year remains unspecified.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Mandatory video, maximum five minutes, responding to one of two problem-solving prompts. Portfolio of up to 20 items is optional but strongly recommended, including non-design work. Programme strongly prefers 2–3 years’ work experience; this is not a published mandatory minimum. Statement, CV, two recommendations and transcripts required. Curriculum: nine credits per semester; transfer credit is not accepted and graduation requires cumulative GPA 3.0. Duration and delivery: 36 credits, two years full-time; New York City campus or online on Eastern-time schedule. Award scope: One MS endpoint; online/on-campus delivery is not counted twice. The separate executive Strategic Design for Global Leadership degree is not this programme. Preparation/recognition: No mandatory academic design-foundation bridge published. Optional ESL study is a language pathway, not degree-subject conversion. No regulated professional licence established. Programme-specific accordion content was verified in the official page’s publicly delivered HTML data. Personal eligibility: Personal eligibility remains unassessed: degree length/country/equivalence, grades, creative or computing work, employment, citizenship, English evidence, budget and intended intake are unknown.

sections.text: 2027 programme requires a bachelor degree or international equivalent with GPA at least 5.0/7.0 and no specified prior discipline. sections.label: Field
sections.text: Environmental policy / natural-resource management / sustainability and water systems

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English proficiency is required for all applicants. Current central page accepts qualifying English education or specified tests but its linked numerical policy returned 404. Historical official 2025 Science guide gives IELTS Academic 6.5 with all components 6.0; that is a reference only, not verified 2027 policy. Current scores, exemptions and test-version rules must be rechecked; no lower pre-sessional score substituted.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Two years, 96 units, in person. Non-cognate entrants are advised to consider including two enabling courses in their first year; these are within the course-selection structure, not a separately guaranteed pre-master admission bridge. No mandatory experience, portfolio or fixed environmental credit minimum is listed for standard entry. Maths is absent from the published cognate-credit list, so do not assume 24/48 units of advanced standing. Bridge and recognition: Recommended enabling modules within first-year studies; no extra compulsory pre-master year published. Transcript-based course prerequisites still require checking. Award structure: One ANU Master of Environment, CRICOS 082293C. Scope caveats: Standard Master of Environment is one endpoint. The Advanced research award and transfer pathway are not separately added. Possible later Advanced transfer requires at least 70% weighted average in initial 48 units, approved supervisor, required courses and that award’s admission conditions; no guaranteed research/PhD route. Cognate discipline credit and recommended enabling courses are separate from initial admission. No regulated professional licence follows automatically; environmental specialisations are not separate master endpoints. Unassessed: citizenship, degree country/equivalence, transcript, GPA, language evidence, budget and intended intake are unknown.
