sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Spring 2027 general international application and uploads: 5 August 2026 09:00 to 14 August 2026 18:00 KST, closed; recommendations by 24:00 KST on closing day. Programme begins early February 2027. Future application round not verified. Scholarship consideration used the same expired application deadline.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Current programme-page tuition, checked 1 October 2026: KRW 28,000,000 for the degree, four full-time instalments of KRW 7,000,000. Page states no further tuition fees for first two years after this total is paid; beyond two years, KRW 300,000/credit. No nationality tuition split shown. Dated 2027 committee notice is expressly Korean-only, so an exact 2027 international invoice remains unverified. Application fee and any other compulsory institutional extras are unverified, not assumed zero. Scholarship route is described in shared KDI conditions; self-funded tuition is substantial. Housing, food, travel, visa and insurance are additional. Funding: Competitive KDIS Scholarship includes full tuition, monthly stipend and institutional support; select KDIS category in admission application. All admitted students considered, committee decides. Prior Korean-government scholarship at the same degree tier bars repeat funding. International nationality/parental-nationality restrictions apply; Korean dual citizenship is excluded from this route. G20/EU nationals except Korea may be considered for Seoul G20. Amount, payment months, travel/housing coverage and 2027 certificate-specific conditions remain unverified. Retention and insurance: 2026 Fall handbook: scholarship-specific GPA threshold is in the award certificate; normally at least nine regular credits per term including three daytime credits, except final fourth term. Do not import PhD GPA rules. Medical insurance is compulsory; 2026 handbook estimates National Health Insurance at approximately KRW 80,000/month; this is not a guaranteed 2027 charge.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Spring-2027 international rules allow an accredited bachelor of at least three years, or legislatively recognised equivalent, without a subject restriction. Shorter first degrees require another bachelor/master to reach cumulative three-year post-secondary study. This supports a plausible mathematics route, not automatic admission.

sections.text: Public policy; economics, regional/environment and social policy

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English teaching. IELTS 6.0, TOEFL iBT 72 (4 for tests from 21 January 2026), OPIc IM3, TEPS 286 or Duolingo 100; tests within two years. Only listed majority-English-speaking nationality/degree-country exemptions; a generic medium-of-instruction certificate is rejected.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Programme fit explicitly includes mathematics coursework and describes 3–7 years in public-sector/related work. These are programme-fit descriptions; the 2027 eligibility section specifies no formal minimum work years, subject ECTS or numerical GPA floor. Relevant experience/background, records, recommendations, statement and interview remain part of competitive assessment. See shared KDI conditions and conflicts. The guide requests employment certification only for applicants who have professional experience. International-applicant nationality/parental-nationality conditions and the exclusion of Korean dual citizenship also require individual checking. Official degree-completion timing is unresolved as recorded below. Duration and delivery: Four academic terms, approximately 1.5 years; about one year/three terms at KDI School in Sejong, then graduation research in the home country, subject to scholarship conditions. International full-time route studied. Any form of employment during the stay is prohibited for full-time students; part-time route is limited to foreign residents working in Korea, without student-visa/financial support. Award scope: KDI School of Public Policy and Management; Master of Public Policy (MPP). Distinct from existing MDS endpoint; concentrations and scholarship schemes do not add endpoints. Verification caveats: 2027 guide says completed certificate before applying but also states 31 August 2026 for other applicants, after the 14 August deadline. Treat degree completion timing as unresolved; Korean/Japanese expected-graduate exceptions have separate Feb/Mar 2027 deadlines. 2027 guide says minimum 36 graduation credits, while current MPP page says 39. Retain both; incoming-cohort curriculum needs confirmation. No mandatory pre-master bridge verified. No user citizenship, degree duration, professional experience or scholarship eligibility assumed. Only one KDI programme application per admissions cycle. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no user citizenship, fee residency, degree/transcript/GPA, work experience, budget, language exemption, intake or individual admission/funding outcome inferred.

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Winter entry. DAAD's dated 2026/27 listing gives 7 May–15 July 2026 for German, EU and non-EU applicants. The faculty describes the recurring portal window as early June–15 July. The shared closing date has passed; no 2027/28 dated call or late-entry opportunity verified.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: The January 2026 examination regulations explicitly accept a single-subject mathematics bachelor's: at least six semesters and 180 ECTS within the EU, or an equivalent foreign degree. For a multi-subject bachelor's, one listed relevant subject must comprise at least 60 ECTS and a second listed subject at least 15 ECTS. Mathematics is explicitly listed; the separate 60-ECTS cognitive-content test concerns unlisted subjects.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Cognitive science / neuroscience / mind and language / cognitive AI

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English teaching; optional German electives. Current regulations specify B2+, including IELTS 6.5 with every component at least 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 85 with every component at least 18. Certificates normally must be at most two years old. Specified native-language and recent completed English-medium degree exemptions may apply. Use these programme-specific regulations over DAAD's generic B2 label; a new-scale 2026 TOEFL equivalence was not verified.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Degree equivalence and eligibility are assessed by the examination board. Four semesters, 120 ECTS. The 2025/26 curriculum includes introductory cognitive science, philosophical methods, programming and statistics; core study in mind/language, brain/behaviour and computation/AI; two focus areas, research practice and a 30-ECTS thesis. Relevant prior training can replace one methods module with electives. This is distinct from RUB's Psychology master's with a cognitive-neuroscience specialisation.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Current published application JPY 30,000; admission JPY 282,000; tuition JPY 642,960/year. Two-year tuition calculation JPY 1,285,920; base academic/application total JPY 1,597,920 before transaction/handling, insurance, living/travel and future increases. Overseas self/external-funded applicants require financial evidence; university first-year tuition/living estimate JPY 2,800,000. Scholarships are competitive and limited, not an automatic net-price reduction. Scholarship option MEXT University Recommendation via GRIPS (October 2027): Deadline: Online November 20, 2026 17:00 JST; documents November 27, 2026 17:00 JST. Conditions: Verified GRIPS AY2027 summary: under 35 on April 1, 2027 and nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan. Funding is competitive and limited. Full controlling 2027 MEXT university-recommendation rules and the precise GRIPS allocation category were not independently located: GPA conversion/minimum, prior-major/research-field relatedness, nationality/dual-nationality details, residence/current study, prior awards, other funding and visa conditions remain unresolved. Do not infer MEXT eligibility from GRIPS any-major admission or apply 2026 rules as if they are 2027 rules. No automatic net tuition reduction. Coverage: JPY 147,000/month; application/admission/tuition; economy airfare home-country–Japan–home on standard-period completion. Exact personal living gap remains. Funding availability update: Current GRIPS notice says 2027 MEXT funding remains available to MP1 and MP2, while certain other programs are affected by planned General Category discontinuation; annual budget formal decision remains pending. Scholarship option ADB–Japan Scholarship Program via GRIPS (October 2027): Deadline: Online November 20, 2026 17:00 JST; documents November 27, 2026 17:00 JST. Conditions: Verified GRIPS AY2027 chart: under 36 on April 1, 2027; nationality of ADB developing member country; two full-time post-bachelor professional years by application deadline; no existing master’s degree or graduate-degree enrollment. Current ADB provider additionally requires borrowing-member/Japanese-ODA eligibility, no developed-country dual citizenship, superior academic record (no numerical GPA threshold stated on this provider page), good health, home-country residence/work, return and work there for at least two years, and exclusions for ADB staff/consultants/close relatives and designated-institution staff. ADB’s age rule is at most 35 at application, with exceptional government-approved waiver: retain both date tests. These restrictions do not define ordinary MP2 academic admission. Coverage: JPY 147,000/month, all three academic/application fees, return economy airfare, health/overseas insurance; establishment JPY 25,000; MP2 research JPY 70,000 year 1 / 42,000 year 2; books JPY 75,000/65,000; travel expenses JPY 25,000. Competitive allocation, not automatic. Compulsory insurance: National Health Insurance premium is household-income based. GRIPS automatically enrolls students in Inbound Futai Gakuso, with sponsor exceptions; separate current premium/payment responsibility not quantified on retrieved page. University example living budget includes JPY 3,000/month for health, accident and property insurance. Do not count it twice. Published living categories total a calculated JPY149,000–316,800/month: rent 35000–106800+utilities 12000–25000+food 40000–80000+transport 8000–15000+insurance 3000+books 5000+phone/internet 6000–12000+leisure 20000+miscellaneous 20000–50000. JPY 147,000 MEXT/ADB monthly stipend alone is JPY 2,000 below the lower sum of this illustrative budget; ADB separately covers books/research/insurance so do not treat that gap as its final deficit. Lifestyle/housing/allowances determine actual shortfall. First stipend can arrive late October/mid-November; bring at least two months living funds.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: General master’s eligibility: bachelor’s degree or equivalent. Admissions policy explicitly accepts all undergraduate majors. Current MP2 policy targets, but is not limited to, early/mid-career public officials and researchers. Suitable for a mathematics graduate at subject level; record/research fit and university equivalence still assessed.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Interdisciplinary public policy and quantitative/qualitative policy analysis

sections.label: Language
sections.text: Taught in English. TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic evidence required unless exempt/waived; admission PRIORITY at TOEFL 79/120 or 4.5/6, IELTS 6, not a hard master’s cutoff. Tests under two years old at enrollment. ITP/IELTS General Training not accepted. Automatic exemption for degrees from accredited institutions in USA, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland; other fully English-taught degrees may request waiver with institutional proof. No assumed exemption. Application language: The 2027–28 overseas guide requires English documents; untranslated non-English transcripts/certificates require official originals plus accredited verbatim English translation. Application, statement and MP2 research proposal use designated forms. Admission examination: MP2 policy includes a video interview assessing, among other factors, communication ability in English. General guide says a video-interview invitation is sent if requested by the screening committee; do not assert all applicants are interviewed.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Bachelor or equivalent, assessed during screening; the general admissions policy welcomes all undergraduate majors. MP2 requires graduate-level academic ability, adequate written/spoken English, interest in real policy issues and sustained research ability. No fixed subject-credit minimum, numeric GPA or universal work-years requirement was found. Policy evaluates degree/subjects, work experience if any, recommendations, research originality and real-world relevance, motivation and potential. Research proposal, statement of purpose and two recommendations are required; employed applicants need employment certification, while new graduates/unemployed do not. Prior professor contact is not required. Only one GRIPS program per academic year. Scholarship age, nationality, work, record, prior-field and residence restrictions are separate. Admissions-route linkage: Overseas admission to the English two-year MA is separate from scholarship eligibility and separate from domestic-applicant procedures. MP1 is not this award. Duration and delivery: 2 years, October–September; 40 Japanese credits plus master’s thesis. No ECTS equivalence asserted. In-person Tokyo. These verified procedures are for applicants residing outside Japan. Those currently in Japan OR planning to move there soon may count as domestic and require different guide/procedures; classification must be checked. Japanese students accepted, but international scholarships have separate nationality/residency rules. Award scope: National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies (GRIPS); MA in Public Policy awarded by GRIPS. Only MP2 staged as a candidate. MP1 is a different one-year Master of Public Policy, not the same award; not counted here. Verification caveats: MP2 current program-policy PDF required visual inspection because embedded text extraction omitted most paragraphs; page3 rendered and inspected. Target includes but is not limited to public-sector early/mid-career officials/researchers. General degree page sounds career-targeted; the actual policy and guide establish no universal work-years gate. Funding can still impose two years. MEXT September 29 update supersedes August chart for discontinued programs but expressly preserves MP1/MP2. MP1 not promoted; kept only as award-identity comparison. All personal nationality, grade, prior-degree recognition/length/country, language and work facts remain unknown. Full 2027 MEXT university-recommendation eligibility is not established by the GRIPS summary chart; scholarship prior-field/GPA/residence/history restrictions remain unresolved. No such eligibility is inferred from any-major admission. GRIPS application materials must be in English and prepared solely by the applicant under the overseas guide; official-document/translation requirements remain mandatory. Online registration alone is insufficient: the guide requires supporting-document receipt and official English-test transmission, with specific scan exceptions for academic records and waiver evidence; no walk-in or emailed full dossier substitute. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no user citizenship, fee residency, degree/transcript/GPA, work experience, budget, language exemption, intake or individual admission/funding outcome inferred.

sections.label: Language
sections.text: For non-native English speakers Graduate School generally seeks IELTS Academic 7.0, Duolingo 125, TOEFL 90 pre-21 January 2026 or 5 on new scale. Waiver requires qualifying two years full-time English-medium study in an English-primary country. Admitted international non-native speakers take placement exams even if waived; assigned language classes may add non-degree tuition.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: GRE not required. CV, life-experience statement, purpose statement and two references; academic references mandatory if degree completed within five years. Writing sample 750–2,500 words: new learning-experience essay or work from past five years with context. No mandatory employment or arts portfolio. 30 credits, nine courses plus capstone. Campus seminars in Durham, often evenings; not verified as online. Homepage says two years full-time / two–six part-time; detailed FAQ says minimum four terms full-time and ten terms part-time, maximum four/six years. Treat duration as study-load-dependent. Academic master, not professional licence. Scope caveats: Duke duration summaries differ; specific FAQ and individual study plan control, rather than assuming a guaranteed two-year part-time route. Fee year explicitly retained; 2026/27 rate covers Spring 2027 but is not a whole-degree price guarantee. Student immigration/full-time requirements require separate verification.

records.institution: KDI School of Public Policy and Management
records.field: International development; sustainable development and impact evaluation

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: Spring 2027 general international application and uploads: 5 August 2026 09:00 to 14 August 2026 18:00 KST, closed; recommendations by 24:00 KST on closing day. Programme begins early February 2027. Future application round not verified. Scholarship consideration used the same expired application deadline.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Current programme-page tuition, checked 1 October 2026: KRW 28,000,000 for the degree, four full-time instalments of KRW 7,000,000. Page states no further tuition fees for first two years after this total is paid; beyond two years, KRW 300,000/credit. No nationality tuition split shown. Dated 2027 committee notice is expressly Korean-only, so an exact 2027 international invoice remains unverified. Application fee and any other compulsory institutional extras are unverified, not assumed zero. Scholarship route is described in shared KDI conditions; self-funded tuition is substantial. Housing, food, travel, visa and insurance are additional. Funding: Competitive KDIS Scholarship includes full tuition, monthly stipend and institutional support; select KDIS category in admission application. All admitted students considered, committee decides. Prior Korean-government scholarship at the same degree tier bars repeat funding. International nationality/parental-nationality restrictions apply; Korean dual citizenship is excluded from this route. G20/EU nationals except Korea may be considered for Seoul G20. Amount, payment months, travel/housing coverage and 2027 certificate-specific conditions remain unverified. Retention and insurance: 2026 Fall handbook: scholarship-specific GPA threshold is in the award certificate; normally at least nine regular credits per term including three daytime credits, except final fourth term. Do not import PhD GPA rules. Medical insurance is compulsory; 2026 handbook estimates National Health Insurance at approximately KRW 80,000/month; this is not a guaranteed 2027 charge.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Spring-2027 international rules allow an accredited bachelor of at least three years, or legislatively recognised equivalent, without a subject restriction. Shorter first degrees require another bachelor/master to reach cumulative three-year post-secondary study. This supports a plausible mathematics route, not automatic admission.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: International development; sustainable development and impact evaluation

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English teaching. IELTS 6.0, TOEFL iBT 72 (4 for tests from 21 January 2026), OPIc IM3, TEPS 286 or Duolingo 100; tests within two years. Only listed majority-English-speaking nationality/degree-country exemptions; a generic medium-of-instruction certificate is rejected.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Programme fit describes 3–7 years in government, NGOs or international development and a basic economics foundation. These are programme-fit descriptions; the 2027 eligibility section specifies no formal minimum work years, subject ECTS or numerical GPA floor. Relevant experience/background, records, recommendations, statement and interview remain part of competitive assessment. See shared KDI conditions and conflicts. The guide requests employment certification only for applicants who have professional experience. International-applicant nationality/parental-nationality conditions and the exclusion of Korean dual citizenship also require individual checking. Official degree-completion timing is unresolved as recorded below. Duration and delivery: Four academic terms, approximately 1.5 years; about one year/three terms at KDI School in Sejong, then graduation research in the home country, subject to scholarship conditions. International full-time route studied. Any form of employment during the stay is prohibited for full-time students; part-time route is limited to foreign residents working in Korea, without student-visa/financial support. Award scope: KDI School of Public Policy and Management; Master of Development Policy (MDP). Distinct from existing MDS endpoint; concentrations and scholarship schemes do not add endpoints. Verification caveats: 2027 guide says completed certificate before applying but also states 31 August 2026 for other applicants, after the 14 August deadline. Treat degree completion timing as unresolved; Korean/Japanese expected-graduate exceptions have separate Feb/Mar 2027 deadlines. No mandatory pre-master bridge verified. No user citizenship, degree duration, professional experience or scholarship eligibility assumed. Only one KDI programme application per admissions cycle. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no user citizenship, fee residency, degree/transcript/GPA, work experience, budget, language exemption, intake or individual admission/funding outcome inferred.

records.field: Digital curation, research data stewardship and digital assets

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: UCT 2027 application page says coursework postgraduate applications close 30 September; interpreted in its April-2026 opening context as 30 September 2026, already past. Programme-specific deadline/late availability not independently recovered. No verified open 2027 round or 2028 dates.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Exact programme tuition remains unverified; the official 2026 Fees Handbook could not be retrieved in the independent web check. UCT charges by course. Non-SADC coursework students additionally face international term fees and an annual non-refundable administration fee, with category-specific rules. The first-payment document currently served at a 2025-named URL is titled 2027 Fees and Payment Dates: South African citizens/permanent residents and SADC students have ZAR 36,000 tuition first payment (or full fee if lower); SADC administration ZAR 5,800 extra. Full-time international coursework/dissertation master students have a ZAR 84,800 initial-payment benchmark. These amounts are expressly not full tuition or whole-degree costs. Applicable residence first payments, travel, contact-session living and offshore fee treatment remain separate/unresolved. Final balance is due 31 July 2027; initial due date is 29 January 2027 for SA citizens/permanent residents and before registration or that date, whichever earlier, for international categories. A one-off 5% surcharge applies to overdue unpaid first-payment amounts. Applicant category and any admission offer remain unassessed. No guaranteed scholarship or applicable funding deadline verified.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: 2026 Humanities handbook expressly accepts a good Honours degree or HEQSF level-8 equivalent in any field, at least 65%, with Head-of-Department recommendation. Maths satisfies the discipline rule only if the qualification and grades meet that level. An ordinary three-year bachelor must not be assumed equivalent. No automatic bridge to this endpoint verified.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Digital curation, research data stewardship and digital assets

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English. Central current minimum is IELTS Academic 6.5 overall/6.0 per component with tests no more than two years old. Humanities FAQ says IELTS 7.0/6.0 and older test-validity wording; its currency and programme-specific application are unresolved. Do not treat central minimum as proof a lower faculty threshold applies, or the older FAQ validity as current permission. Confirm the Digital Curation requirement; higher 7.0 is a conservative preparation target, not a newly verified programme rule.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: No mandatory prior professional work or creative portfolio stated in programme entry clause. HOD approval and faculty rules apply; required application documents/research preparation need confirmation. Coursework must be passed before dissertation registration. Distinct taught digital-curation curriculum, not the LIS-restricted MLIS or dissertation-only MPhil. Duration and delivery: 192 NQF credits: three taught courses totalling 96 plus 96-credit minor dissertation. Department flyer describes one or two years by blended delivery with one/two contact sessions; 2027 timetable and attendance arrangements unverified. Optional Curating in Context includes a one-month on-site experience. Do not describe as fully online. The generic faculty FAQ says no online/distance postgraduate degrees, while the programme flyer describes blended attendance; this does not establish fully remote access. Confirm current contact requirements with the department. Award scope: University of Cape Town; MPhil specialising in Digital Curation, LIS04, HEQSF/NQF level 9. No other UCT digital-curation endpoint was found in the catalogue. Professional recognition: An academic/professional-skills MPhil in digital stewardship. Specific external professional accreditation and any regulated licence pathway were not verified; do not market it as librarian registration. Verification caveats: Department flyer and clone webpage say 60%; 2026 handbook says 65% in any field. Use current handbook 65% screen and disclose conflict. Honours/level-8 equivalence is an actual entry gate. Language sources conflict; central minimum is not proof that a lower faculty threshold applies. Initial payment must never be stored as total tuition. The independently reopened first-payment PDF is labelled 2027 and replaces the staging draft’s 2026 payment figures; its old filename is not the fee year. Full tuition is still unknown. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no assumption about degree equivalence, grades, citizenship/residency, experience, English, budget, visa eligibility or admission.

## 4. Saarland University, Germany — MSc Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
- Fit: English; 120 credits/two years; application areas include language, physics, materials, psychology and biology. sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: October admission. Last complete general call: March 25–April 8, 2026 online filing; EXPIRED. Results May 20, 2026; arrival no later than October 1, 2026. AY 2027 guide expected November 2026; application period described as March 2027, without exact dates yet. Preserve 2026 criteria as last published, subject to announced 2027 process changes.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: AY 2026 application JPY 30,000 plus remittance; entrance JPY 282,000; tuition JPY 535,800/year. Calculated two-year tuition JPY 1,071,600; tuition+entrance+application JPY 1,383,600 before insurance/handling/living. No residency/nationality tuition surcharge specified. Funding and housing explicitly not guaranteed. Scholarship option ADB–Japan Scholarship Program at GSICS (October 2026): Deadline: January 5–13, 2026 registered-post receipt; EXPIRED. Eligibility inquiries by December 5, 2025. Successful nominees online registration/payment by April 8, 2026. AY 2027 call not found.. Conditions: Both GSICS admission and ADB requirements apply: ADB borrowing/Japanese ODA-eligible citizenship, no developed-country dual citizenship, superior bachelor record, two full-time professional years after degree, age at most 35 at application, English proficiency, residence/work in home country, no current graduate enrollment, no designated-institution staff or ADB staff/close relatives. Under 16 years schooling needed advance eligibility review. Return/work at home at least two years; provider health condition. Coverage: Provider covers full tuition, subsistence including housing, books, medical insurance and travel; no current Kobe-specific stipend amount verified. Local call explicitly requires JPY 30,000 application fee from successful applicants; do not silently treat it as waived or assume reimbursement. Competitive selection. Compulsory extras: two-year PAS accident insurance JPY1,750; annual IMAS assistance JPY1,980 plus JPY210 handling per payment. International students also require Inbound Futai Gakusou comprehensive insurance and National Health Insurance. Exact current comprehensive premium unresolved: university still links a table dated September 25, 2020 (two-year types vary), so do not call that a confirmed AY 2027 quote. NHI living estimate JPY 2,000/month. Measles/rubella certificate requirement can add testing/vaccination cost. Living budget: university says around JPY100,000/month or more; A broad estimate, not a guaranteed minimum. Listed private-rent components sum to about JPY 127,000–132,000 before deposits; dorms can be cheaper. Page totals are accommodation-dependent. Housing deposits, travel, immigration costs and other study costs remain extra.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Last complete guide is AY2026, not AY2027. Its common general-admission degree routes contain no specified bachelor-major restriction and expressly apply to the English Special Course for Development Policy, whose available awards include Master of International Studies. Mathematics is therefore a plausible prior subject, conditional on degree recognition, research fit and competitive selection. No personal admission eligibility is established; complete AY2027 requirements are still unverified.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: AY2026 common general gate: recognized qualifying degree/education route; adequate English; research proposal, academic records and recommendation. Categories (6) foreign three-year-or-longer degree, (7) professional-college, (8) minister-approved and (9) individual-equivalence applicants needed advance review documents by February 4, 2026. Category (9) required age 22 by September 30, 2026. No numeric GPA, prior subject-credit or work-years minimum was stated. Policy assesses international-cooperation understanding, motivation, intercultural competence and research aptitude. AY2026 general applicants needed supervisor consent; official AY2027 notice removes the consent letter and introduces an online interview after document screening. Do not apply the remaining AY2026 dossier rules automatically to AY2027. Degree-route details: (1) accredited Japanese university graduation by end September 2026; (2) statutory bachelor under School Education Act Article 104.4 by end September 2026; (3) completion of 16 years education outside Japan by end September 2026; (4) 16 years foreign correspondence education while in Japan by end September 2026; (5) minister-approved foreign-system university in Japan with at least 16 years education, graduation by end September 2026; (6) accredited/designated overseas bachelor-equivalent program requiring at least three years, including specified distance/foreign-system provision; advance eligibility review; (7) minister-recognized specialized training college postsecondary course at least four years and prescribed requirements; advance review; (8) minister-recognized qualification under Notice No. 5 of 1953; advance review; (9) GSICS individual academic-equivalence recognition and at least age 22 by September 30, 2026; advance review. Admissions-route linkage: October English Special Course for Development Policy is expressly linked to Master of International Studies in AY2026 guide sections 1–2. The admissions landing page directly links that guide and publishes AY2027 changes. The four named programs on the school overview are labelled as the April Japanese-taught route; do not recast them as separate English endpoints. English course departments are DEDP, DICPS and DRCPS; they are not counted as extra degrees. Exact individual department/award allocation and full AY2027 criteria remain unverified. Duration and delivery: Normally 2 years; 30 Japanese credits, English thesis and final interview. 2026 admissions guide allows exceptional one-year completion, whereas education page describes at least two years: use two-year normal budget; no acceleration assumed. No ECTS conversion asserted. Award scope: Kobe University; Master of International Studies, delivered through GSICS Special Course for Development Policy (October English-taught route). Verification caveats: 2027 process change supersedes 2025 FAQ/2026 supervisor-consent advice: consent no longer required; online interview added. English-course 2026 general document list should not be silently rolled forward to 2027. No personal degree recognition, language or scholarship eligibility assumed. Exact endpoint narrowed to Master of International Studies via the shared English course; no English International Studies Program title is invented. AY2027 online interview language is not specified by the brief change notice; retain this unknown. University legacy course page mentions an AY2015 intake and omits Political Science from its award list. Use it only for English-teaching corroboration; AY2026 admissions guide controls current award linkage. Personal eligibility: Unassessed: no user citizenship, fee residency, degree/transcript/GPA, work experience, budget, language exemption, intake or individual admission/funding outcome inferred.

## 1. ETH Zurich, Switzerland — MSc Data Science
- Fit: Mathematics is explicitly a qualifying bachelor's discipline. This is a selective specialized degree, not a CS conversion course; detailed prerequisite matching is needed. English; 120 ECTS / two years; includes a practical interdisciplinary Data Science Laboratory.

**Route:** Ten-month professional coursework/capstone degree; direct transition into practical data science/AI if prerequisites met. Okanagan is another separately applied-for campus option.

sections.label: Description
sections.text:
## 4. Cornell — MEng Operations Research and Information Engineering, Ithaca, USA
**Route:** Professional engineering degree explicitly welcoming mathematics graduates; optimization, logistics, data analytics, manufacturing, finance and operational decisions. Usually two semesters; financial engineering is three semesters. Design project rather than research thesis.
**Background:** Calculus including multivariable/vector calculus, linear algebra, calculus-based probability/statistics and intermediate programming. Financial engineering adds probability/statistical theory and finance prerequisites; economics alone does not replace finance. English proficiency requirement applies when not exempt.
**Deadline:** Standing departmental Fall deadline December 1; exact 2027 cycle label not shown. Spring entry restricted to Cornell undergraduates.
**Cost/funding:** Self-funded Tier 1 professional tuition. Exact 2026/27 numeric rate not reliably extracted; use linked current schedule rather than research-MS pricing. Selective full/partial tuition fellowships; GTRS work awards do not include a tuition waiver.

records.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Planetary Geosciences (GeoPlaNet)
records.institution: Nantes Université / Universidade de Coimbra / Università degli Studi G. d’Annunzio Chieti-Pescara

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: September 2026 fourth-cohort application period is explicitly closed. Published funding table covers four cohorts through 2026/27; 2027 intake, renewal and scholarships unverified. Historical final-year route required graduation by 31 July and degree certificate by 31 August.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Published scheme averages 15 EMJM scholarships/cohort, up to EUR 1,400/month over 24 months while participating; awardees pay no registration fee, insurance covered. Non-awardees: about EUR 4,000/year (EUR 8,000/two years), plus travel, visa, installation and living; programme covers insurance. Figures are not a 2027 quote. Scholarship conditions: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (Four cohorts 2023–2026 entry; 2026 application closed): No prior EMJM scholarship; maximum six awards per nationality over the four cohorts; continuous programme involvement required. 2027 renewal unverified.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Mathematics expressly accepted among science degrees. Recognised tertiary qualification equivalent to at least 180 ECTS required; admission is selective.

sections.label: Field
sections.text: Planetary geosciences and space exploration

sections.label: Language
sections.text: English B2. Programme gives IELTS range 5–6.5 with every component at least 5.0; exact accepted-test equivalence needs checking, not a guaranteed IELTS 5.0 offer. Native-English or fully English-taught higher-education degree can qualify for exemption with required evidence.

sections.label: Prerequisites
sections.text: Academic record, motivation, two references and shortlisted interview assessed. No mandatory work, portfolio or quantified prior geoscience credits stated. Non-EHEA qualifications need apostille/legalisation before programme start; translations required subject to listed language exceptions. Mobility and residence: Semester 1 Coimbra, semester 2 Chieti-Pescara, semester 3 Nantes, semester 4 worldwide partner internship. Physical mobility and visas required; residence-sensitive EMJM rules need individual confirmation. Award structure: Joint Erasmus Mundus Master Degree in Planetary Geosciences – GeoPlaNet from the three partners, plus diploma supplement; jointly accredited under national titles in France (Sciences de la Terre et des Planètes, Environnement), Italy (Laurea Magistrale Internazionale in Planetary Sciences) and Portugal (Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Planetary Geosciences). One integrated route, not three additional programme endpoints. Scope caveats: Programme funding page dated 21 October 2025 has a remaining-nationality table for 2026, including inconsistent duplicated Italy rows. Do not turn that table into current personal eligibility. Separate ESA Academy support shown for 2024–26 and proposed 2025–27 is historical/conditional and is not counted as a new 2027 award. Standalone partner masters do not automatically receive this EMJM grant.

sections.label: Description
sections.text:
## 10. Georgia Tech — Professional MS Bioinformatics, USA
**Route:** Interdisciplinary route into computational biology/genomics and health-related data work; professional, three-semester degree, 36 credits, research/internship opportunities.
**Background:** Explicitly admits mathematics bachelor's graduates, but also expects introductory biology covering cells, molecules, genetics and evolution, plus introductory CS/programming and calculus/linear algebra. This is a prerequisite-dependent pivot, not automatic direct access from a math-only transcript.
**Deadline:** Standing December 1 early consideration, March 1 final for Fall entry; exact 2027 label not shown.
**Cost/funding:** Fall2026 out-of-country tuition USD20,825 per semester at 12+ credits, USD1,736/credit below that load, plus fees. 2027 and total program cost not separately verified. After first semester, competitive computational-biology GRA awards can include tuition waiver/stipend; do not budget on winning one.
Sources: [admissions/background/funding](https://www.bioinformatics.gatech.edu/index.php/professional-masters-admission [curriculum](https://catalog.gatech.edu/programs/bioinformatics-ms/bioinformatics-ms.pdf [Fall2026 tuition](https://bursar.gatech.edu/student/tuition/fa26/fa26_totals_page.pdf

## Important exclusions and application traps
- Pure mathematics intentionally excluded.
- Colorado State's funded Statistics MS/PhD is explicitly designed for PhD-seeking students rather than terminal-MS applicants; it should not be presented as a normal funded standalone master's. [Official FAQ](https://statistics.colostate.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16/2024/08/frequently-asked-questions-msphd-1.pdf
- Penn's official catalog says Fall2026 is the last new MCIT cohort and Fall2027 replaces it with Master of Applied Science in Computer Science. Verify the new program before recommending the old MCIT name. [Official catalog](https://catalog.upenn.edu/graduate/programs/computer-information-technology-mcit/
- A strong math background makes data science, OR, quantitative finance and statistics natural transitions, but coding, domain prerequisites and degree equivalence remain decisive. Conversion routes solve missing foundation problems at potentially substantial extra cost.

sections.label: Description
sections.text:
## 8. UBC — MA Economics, Canada
**Route:** Graduate economics, quantitative policy/empirical research; explicitly accepts mathematics and other STEM graduates without economics degrees. Not a guarantee that no economics preparation is needed.
**Background:** Strong applicants have intermediate microeconomics, two semesters statistics/econometrics and calculus; linear algebra/multivariable calculus recommended. Department evaluates non-economics applicants' quantitative training. English proficiency where applicable. Separate Economics and Computation stream requires CS-degree-equivalent coursework, so a math degree alone is insufficient for that stream.
**Deadline:** Standing December 15 application, January 12 documents; 2027-specific label not confirmed. Main program approximately one year, thesis route can extend.
**Cost/funding:** Current international annual tuition CAD32,393.73 plus fees; 2027 rate not separately confirmed. Scholarships/tuition awards/TAships competitive, not guaranteed to every admit.
Sources: [MA admissions and structure](https://economics.ubc.ca/graduate/masters-program/ [international tuition](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/graduate-degree-programs/master-of-arts-economics [funding](https://economics.ubc.ca/graduate/masters-program/masters-funding/ [computation-stream gate](https://economics.ubc.ca/graduate/masters-program/ec-stream/

sections.label: Admissions
sections.text: The 2026/27 call names both Science Education master and standalone PGDip, with September/October 2026 commencement and 30 September 2026 deadline. That deadline has passed. No subsequent opening, late application permission or next master cohort after a future diploma is established.

sections.label: Cost Funding
sections.text: Master tuition: LKR 300,000 local in curriculum and current call. Curriculum foreign price USD 2,000 conflicts with current call saying foreign programme fees are double local, implying LKR 600,000. Obtain a fee-category quote before budgeting. Local diploma plus selected Master arithmetic is LKR 425,000 before extras, future revisions and possible call-specific discounts. No guaranteed scholarship. Published extras in LKR, local/foreign: application 2000/4000; registration 5000/10000; refundable lending-library 2000/4000 and science deposit 1500/3000; nonrefundable reference-library 1500/3000; medical 500/1000. Annual renewal after GPA release is stated as 2000, without a separate foreign amount. Resits and other contingencies cost extra. Programme fee includes ordinary examination fee according to the central schedule. The 2026/27 call advertises a 10% course-fee discount for local students in Sri Lanka paying the SLQF 9/10 course fee fully at registration. It is not assumed applicable to the user, the standalone PGDip, a later cohort or all extra fees.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: Programme entry requires a BSc AND either a Postgraduate Diploma in Science Education/Education OR equivalent qualifications/experience acceptable to PGIS in place of that education preparation. The equivalence alternative is not treated as permission to waive the separately stated BSc requirement. Selection tests aptitude, English and subject knowledge, followed by interview. The explicit Mathematics Education component is an education specialism, not a pure-mathematics degree. A mathematics BA is not assumed equivalent to the specified BSc. Shared institutional recognition and relevant-subject assessment remain.

Published A/B/C packages list TRY 45,000/36,000/27,000 stipends for nine months of the year, single/double dormitory accommodation subject to availability or TRY 12,000 transportation subsidy, year-round private health insurance, a computer, and conference support at least once when presenting thesis-related work. AKIS eligible funding from October 2026: tuition waiver plus ILS 3,510/month, at most 24 months; full award includes international health insurance. Year two requires all academic requirements, at least 21 required/elective credits (50%), minimum average 85, and detailed proposal approval during year one. Security, housing, travel and living are additional. Competitive 2026/27 Excellence stipend ILS 4,563 plus tuition, approved housing and international insurance had a 31 July 2026 deadline, now past. Neither award is guaranteed.

intake_deadlines.text: Explicit 2027 dates and applicant categories are preserved below. Do not assign a category or roll forward TBC/unknown dates.

structured_detail.note: At-home/online tests are not accepted. Tests must be completed within two years of course start. TOEFL tests taken on or after 21 January 2026 must be TOEFL iBT Australia; results on the 1–6 scale are not accepted. Separate recognised-prior-study routes exist with timing, English-medium, recognition and evidence requirements; RMIT makes the final assessment. Domestic applicants also meet university minimum English requirements.
structured_detail.other_prior_study_routes: Outside the recognised-country list, fully English-taught/assessed study can be considered for IELTS-6.5-or-lower courses: one year equivalent Diploma-or-higher tertiary study within two years; one full-time postgraduate semester within two years; RMIT-recognised bachelor-or-higher within five years; or recognised senior-secondary qualification within two years unless otherwise stated. Listed-country schooling route requires six years primary/secondary, including two secondary/senior-secondary, entirely English-taught/assessed with required final English results and proof. Specific alternatives and regional recognition rules remain RMIT-assessed; most recent evidence normally controls.
structured_detail.prior_study_route_example: For study in a country outside RMIT’s recognised-English-speaking-country list, a recognised bachelor or higher completed within five years may support English compliance for a course requiring IELTS 6.5 or lower if fully taught and assessed in English. An official institution letter may be required; RMIT makes the final decision and normally considers only the most recent English evidence. This is a possible route, not a personal waiver.

language.text: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0. Other published alternatives and conditions are retained in structured detail; no individual exemption assumed. Current RMIT policy confirms the published 79 TOEFL requirement is on the Australia version: from 21 January 2026 it rejects the 1–6-scale version. Test validity is two years before course start; approved prior-study routes are conditional.

work_selection.text: No work experience required for standard two-year degree. Domestic advanced standing can use any degree plus two relevant years. International advanced-standing block lists business/related degree or RMIT graduate certificate, so do not carry domestic work option across. International block requires qualification completed within last 10 years. Domestic block allows older qualification with evidence of ongoing relevant work/professional development.

sections.label: Eligibility
sections.text: accepted bachelor subjects: The admissions guide welcomes law, natural sciences, engineering and other disciplines with convincing motivation. Regulation §4(1)(1) names law, engineering, natural sciences, economic/business sciences, media or literature studies, or comparable subjects, with equivalent domestic/foreign first professional university qualifications or other equivalent qualifications. Mathematics/applied mathematics is not expressly named and must not be treated as automatically satisfying the natural-science or comparable-subject category.; degree equivalence: The standard route requires a bachelor or equivalent first qualifying degree with at least 240 ECTS. Under §4(2), the study and examination committee decides comparability of programmes, equivalence of foreign university degrees and the overall foreign grade; it may consult the German Central Office for Foreign Education. Nominal four-year duration is not itself a guarantee of 240-ECTS equivalence.; formal gate note: Treat committee-approved subject comparability, foreign-degree/grade equivalence, prior-credit sufficiency, relevant qualified experience and English evidence as separate gates. A persuasive motivation statement does not waive the formal regulation.; grade: No fixed numeric entrance-grade floor located in the current admission guide or regulation §4. Grade conversion sheet, transcripts and ranking evidence are required; selection and academic quality still matter. The instructions allow an official university confirmation when rankings are not provided.; language: English. Current guide: IELTS Academic ≥6.5, TOEFL iBT ≥85 on published older scale, Cambridge C1 ≥185; tests within three years. Native English/English-medium degree exemptions subject to evidence. Regulation instead names Cambridge CPE grade C and older TOEFL formats; do not silently equate these or invent a new TOEFL-scale conversion.; selection: Motivation, CV, degrees/transcripts, grade-conversion/ranking documents, two recommendations and proof of experience; APS document for specified applicant countries per guide.; shorter degree route: Unresolved for exactly 180 ECTS. The admissions guide permits up to 60 credits for professional experience and describes a three-year degree with two years of experience. The retained consolidated regulation §4(3), PDF page 4, instead explicitly describes fewer than 240 but more than 180 ECTS, plus a further 12 months of qualified professional experience and additional competencies beyond the ordinary 12-month requirement. Its following knowledge-examination alternative concerns proof of the necessary competency level; it does not expressly establish that exactly 180 ECTS is admissible. Neither automatic admission nor categorical rejection of an exactly-180-ECTS applicant is established. That subroute needs authoritative reconciliation.; source ids: MIP-A; MIP-I; MIP-R; subject credits: 240 total prior ECTS standard requirement, rather than a fixed undergraduate law-credit quota. See disputed shortened-credit route below.; work: At least 12 months qualified professional experience after first degree. Guide treats full-time as approximately 35–40 hours/week and part-time pro rata; postgraduate internships/research may count. Regulation requires work applying knowledge/methods from prior study.
